segments.en:

And he asked the administrators of the yeshiva to give me bread for the children

And they said: “No, not to Yisroel Ber, he studies Breslov books, we will not give him anything”

Rav Moshe, Rav Moshe Kliers, yes, afterwards he became ill and passed away

He was the head of the yeshiva, and everything was in the hand, in his hand, yes

{Yes, and that is it, and.. yes, and..}

His administrator said: “Rav Moshe does not want to give them anything, he studies Breslov books in the yeshiva”…

...{He was} a young man of thirty or less, yes, a young man

And he spoke about Rebbe Nassan and about our holy Rabbainu, he spoke lashon hara

Oh, what he suffered, oy vey, oy vey, oy vey, what he saw and what he suffered {for this}

For having disgraced the tzaddik

Who can estimate this?

What he suffered

All, {there was all ..…}, th.. all the dollars of America were in his hand

And I had no bread, no, neither I nor my little children, I had no bread to eat

I do not {...}, I am ashamed to tell it, but the truth is like this

Ah

[……..]…

...I walked from Meah Shearim {….} to Shaarei Chesed with, with, with sick legs, and I asked:

“I need bread for children”

And there was no one who would give me; I, I returned and I had nothing, no bread and no money and nothing

I returned home, and I saw that the children wanted bread and were crying: “Bread, bread, bread”

And there was no one who would have compassion and give me bread, only

There was great danger, we all were, I do not know how I r.., how we remained alive

One child, six years old, sh.. one child, a little child, one child, he m.. died of hunger

translatorChecks.reviewerNotes: Preserved all canonical paragraphs, braces, repetitions, hesitations, false starts, the dangling “only,” and the repeated description of the child. The opening sequence of names is grammatically unclear and remains unsmoothed.

qa.reviewNotes: Corrected after clause-by-clause review. Paragraphs 1–7 retain the unclear opening name sequence, all braces, the repeated Rav Moshe name, ‘in the hand, in his hand,’ the braced false starts, and the quoted refusal. Paragraphs 8–13 preserve ‘thirty or less,’ the repeated young-man description, the lashon-hara clauses, three ‘oy vey’ repetitions, and both short suffering clauses. Paragraphs 14–18 preserve the anomalous dollars construction, all bread negations, the incomplete braced clause, ‘Ah,’ and the bracketed ellipsis. Paragraphs 19–24 retain the threefold ‘with,’ the complete request and failed-return clauses, three cries of ‘Bread,’ the dangling ‘only,’ and the broken danger sentence. In paragraph 25, corrected unsupported expansions of the two Hebrew false starts: ש.. is now conservatively ‘sh..’ rather than ‘wh..,’ and מ.. is ‘m..’ rather than ‘d..’; all repeated references to the child remain. No material was skipped or added.

segments.en:
He became swollen like this and he died

{The heart aches}, my first child, passed away from hunger

Who can estimate? Who can tell?

But this was, now I see that it is good, good and good…

...I tasted the taste, how children cry, {come} and cry: “Bread, bread, bread”

And no, no n.., and I had nothing to give them

This taste is more {than shame}, a little child asks for bread, and I had nothing to give him, like this, a piece of bread, some piece, just a piece, so that he would feel the taste of bread…

...[Rebbe Yisroel, he asks whether “Sichos Haran,” {if\with} “Chayei Moharan”]

Ah?

[Rebbe Yisroel, he asks whether “Sichos Haran”]

“Sichos Haran,” “Chayei Moharan”

[Whether it is like “Likutay Moharan”?]

What there is there, days, the great sea would not provide enough ink to write, to write about, about the greatness of Rabbainu, of blessed memory

That he was i.., in such a world

And I was only {drawn close}, and they said:

“It is forbidden to give him bread for.., it is forbidden to give him bread

He studies all day and all {the night} ‘Likutay Halachos’..”

[…...]

“He studies at night with Rebbe Yisroel ‘Likutay Halachos,’ at night

We study Gemara all day and sleep at night

And they studied ‘Likutay Halachos’ at night, and we sleep

If we had not been sleeping, they would not have allowed them {..} to study ‘Likutay Halachos’..”

But they were sleeping…

...When day came and the children opened their mouths: “Bread, bread, bread”

And I had no bread to give them, oy, what a taste this is

One child, one year old, passed away; then he became swollen, and {the body} became like gold, and became swollen

Until his soul departed, until his soul departed from hunger

Such a thing is not heard of in the world…

translatorChecks.reviewerNotes: Preserved all canonical paragraphs, bracketed turns, braces (including the source alternative {if\with}), repetitions, false starts, quotations, and the account of the child. Source ימים in the great-sea/ink clause appears anomalous and is retained literally as “days” rather than silently normalized.

qa.reviewNotes: Corrected after clause-by-clause review. Paragraphs 1–5 retain the swelling/death account, the braced heartache, both rhetorical questions, ‘good, good and good,’ ‘tasted the taste,’ the braced {come}, and three cries of ‘Bread.’ In paragraph 6, restored the literal repeated ‘no, no,’ preserved נ.. conservatively as ‘n..’ rather than the staging’s unsupported ‘I did not h..,’ and corrected ‘did not have to give’ to ‘had nothing to give’ so the clause does not falsely imply lack of obligation. Paragraph 7 received the same semantic correction (‘had nothing to give him’) while retaining every piece/bread/taste repetition and the brace. Paragraphs 8–12 preserve all bracketed turns, the exact {if\with} source alternative, and book-title quotations. Paragraphs 13–23 retain the anomalous literal ‘days,’ doubled ‘write’ and ‘about,’ the i.. false start, all braces, nested/unmatched quotation oddities, repeated night/study/sleep clauses, and the final ‘But they were sleeping.’ Paragraphs 24–28 preserve the second threefold bread cry, repeated swelling, repeated soul-departure clause, and closing ellipsis. No unsupported stage directions were introduced.
